_source: design/04 §4 + D9. `node tools/type-errors/record.mjs` re-records; the test fails on any drift.

sentence._why: D9 as it applies to OUR branded messages: the sentence inside OrmTypeError<'…'> is the thing a user reads, and it must fit on one terminal line.

diagnostic._why: The whole tsc output for one mistake. D9's evidence is 'ours is 1 line, 293 chars' for E1; the default here allows TypeScript's own one- or two-line elaboration (which is usually the useful part — see op-class-gate) but not a cascade.

invariance-rebind._why: The worst diagnostic in the surface, and knowingly so. TypeScript prints both `Query<…>` operands, each carrying the whole `Schema<…>` type argument, and then reports TS2719 ('two different types with this name') because after truncation they print identically. Lines 3-5 ARE the actionable part: `Property 'email' is missing in type '{ id: UserId; }'`. Kept because the alternative — covariant `O` — produces NO diagnostic at all and a silently wrong result type (kysely.md §1.8 pattern 3); `$if` and `$call` exist so this is reachable only by writing the pattern deliberately.

design04Section4._why: design/04 §4's own head-to-head, so drift against the published claim is visible. Totals across E1+E2+E3, `tsc --pretty false`, TS 5.9.3.
